title: Wait for a worker, but not forever

blocks.text: `join()` waits until a thread ends, and waits **forever** if it never does. The page's safer form is a bounded `join(millis)`, then `isAlive()` to see whether the thread is still running, and `interrupt()` to ask it to stop. Two edge cases from the page matter here: `join()` on a thread that was never started returns at once (it waits only while the thread is alive), and `join(0)` means "wait forever".
Write `Deadline.await(Thread worker, long millis)`, returning an `Outcome`:

items: `NOT_STARTED` if `worker` was never started (do not wait);
`CANCELLED` if it is still running after `millis`: interrupt it first.

cases.says: A worker that ends in time is FINISHED; one still running at the deadline is CANCELLED.
A worker still running at the deadline is interrupted.
A worker that was never started is NOT_STARTED, not FINISHED.
A timeout of 0 or less throws IllegalArgumentException instead of waiting forever.

origin.section: `join()` — Waiting for a Thread to Complete
